title: SWS: 69% of Filipinos aware of flood control probe
summary: Nearly seven in 10 adult Filipinos are aware of investigations into alleged anomalies in flood control projects, up from 48% last year, according to a Social Weather Stations (SWS) survey released…

blocks.text: Published November 24, 2026 7:41pm

Nearly seven in 10 adult Filipinos are aware of investigations into alleged anomalies in flood control projects, up from 48% last year, according to a Social Weather Stations (SWS) survey released Tuesday.

The September 21 to 27, 2026, survey found that 69% of respondents were already aware of the investigations before they were interviewed, while the remaining 31% learned about the probe during the survey.
The awareness rate was highest in Metro Manila at 80%, followed by Balance Luzon at 70%, the Visayas at 69%, and Mindanao at 61%, the SWS said.

Awareness also increased with educational attainment, reaching 83% among college graduates, 78% among those who attended senior high school or college, 73% among junior high school graduates, 59% among elementary graduates, and 43% among those who did not finish elementary school.
Confidence in charges
The survey also found that 41% of adult Filipinos had “much confidence” that people would be charged over corruption linked to the flood control anomalies, resulting in a net confidence score of +8.
This was lower than the +18 recorded in September 2025 and the +9 in November 2025.
Net confidence was highest in Mindanao at +15, followed by Balance Luzon at +10 and the Visayas at +6. Metro Manila, meanwhile, registered a negative net confidence score of -7.
The proportion of respondents with very little confidence was highest among college graduates at 27% and Metro Manila residents at 26%, the SWS said.
Meanwhile, only 28% expected that many or almost all those involved would be jailed, while 38% believed that only a few or hardly anyone would face imprisonment.
The SWS conducted face-to-face interviews with 1,500 adults aged 18 and above nationwide: 600 in Balance Luzon and 300 each in Metro Manila, the Visayas, and Mindanao.
The survey had sampling error margins of ±3 percentage points for national results, ±4 points for Balance Luzon, and ±6 points each for Metro Manila, the Visayas, and Mindanao.

The investigations stemmed from a corruption controversy that erupted in July 2025, when President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., during his fourth State of the Nation Address, ordered a probe into alleged irregularities in government flood control projects.

The controversy intensified after inspections uncovered projects that were either substandard, incomplete or allegedly nonexistent despite having been reported as completed and paid for by the government.

The Senate and House of Representatives subsequently conducted investigations, while Marcos created the Independent Commission for Infrastructure (ICI) in September 2025 to investigate alleged corruption in flood control and other infrastructure projects.

The investigations implicated lawmakers, former government officials, DPWH personnel and contractors in an alleged scheme involving budget insertions, rigged bidding processes and kickbacks from government infrastructure funds.

The Ombudsman has since filed criminal cases against several personalities, including former House Speaker Martin Romualdez, Sen. Jinggoy Estrada, former senator Ramon "Bong" Revilla Jr., former Ako Bicol representative Elizaldy "Zaldy" Co, former DPWH Secretary Manuel Bonoan and contractors Sarah and Curlee Discaya.

As of October 2026, the Ombudsman reported that 39 cases involving 52 individuals had been filed before the courts, including 35 cases before the Sandiganbayan and four before regional trial courts. More cases remained under investigation.
Despite the filing of charges and arrests of several personalities, the criminal proceedings remain ongoing, with no final determination of guilt in these cases.— MCG, GMA News
